releases.name: v0.1.10 — plugin load fix
releases.body:
## The plugin loads again

0.1.8 shipped a broken import: `src/index.ts` used `TODO_STATUSES` and `TODO_PRIORITIES` without importing them, so the plugin failed to load with:

```
ReferenceError: TODO_STATUSES is not defined
failed to load plugin
```

No tool was registered at all — `todo_write` and `todo_read` simply did not exist. Fixed in 0.1.10.

> Note: 0.1.9 never reached the registry (it stayed as a staged publish and cannot be promoted), so this is 0.1.10 with the same fix.

![The /todo dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeonVeganMan/opencode-todo-md/master/screen/todo.png)

## Install

```json
{ "plugins": ["opencode-todo-md"] }
```

The TUI half (sidebar strip and `/todo`) loads at TUI startup: restart `opencode`, or run `/reload`.

## Recap of recent versions

- 0.1.10 — fix the load failure, the plugin registers its tools again
- 0.1.8 — `todo_write` merges by default: items without an `id` are appended, items with an `id` are updated; `mode: "replace"` is the only way to delete tasks
- 0.1.7 — `/todo renumber`, ids rewritten 1..N by priority and due date
- 0.1.6 / 0.1.5 — `ctrl+n` creates a task, `ctrl+e` opens the selected task in the editor

58 unit tests. MIT.

releases.name: v0.1.9 — plugin load fix
releases.body:
## Plugin did not load at all

0.1.8 declared the tool input schema with `TODO_STATUSES` and `TODO_PRIORITIES` but never imported them, so the server half threw on load:

```
ReferenceError: TODO_STATUSES is not defined
failed to load plugin target=...opencode-todo-md
```

No tools were registered: `todo_write` and `todo_read` were simply missing. 0.1.9 imports both constants.

### Install

```json
{ "plugins": ["opencode-todo-md"] }
```

The TUI half (sidebar strip and `/todo`) loads at TUI startup: restart `opencode`, or run `/reload`.

### Everything from 0.1.8 is included

- `todo_write` merges by default: items without an `id` are appended, items with an `id` are updated.
- `mode: "replace"` is the only way to delete tasks; an empty list clears the file.
- Stable ids, priorities, due dates, completion dates, tags, `/todo renumber`, `/todo import`.

58 unit tests. MIT.

releases.name: v0.1.8 — todo_write merges by default
releases.body:
Fixes a data-loss bug: `todo_write` treated every write as the complete list, so a single-item write could wipe the rest of `TODO.md`.

Now it merges by default: items without an `id` are appended, items with an `id` update that task, and nothing is deleted. A patch list (`[{ "id": 3, "status": "completed" }]`) changes only the given fields. `mode: "replace"` is the only way to delete, and an empty list clears the file.

![The /todo dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeonVeganMan/opencode-todo-md/master/screen/todo.png)

```json
{ "plugins": ["opencode-todo-md"] }
```

Restart `opencode` (or `/reload`) after installing: the TUI half loads at startup.

**New in 0.1.8**

- merge is the default write mode; partial writes can no longer delete tasks
- patch mode for id-based updates
- `mode: "replace"` for deletions, empty list to clear
- the tool returns the list actually stored in `TODO.md`

58 unit tests. MIT.

releases.name: v0.1.5 — ctrl+e
releases.body:
![The /todo dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeonVeganMan/opencode-todo-md/master/screen/todo.png)

A project todo list for OpenCode, stored in a plain `TODO.md` and shared by every session of the project.

## Install

```json
{
  "plugins": ["opencode-todo-md"]
}
```

Restart the TUI or run `/reload` after installing: the TUI half of a plugin is loaded at process start.

## New in 0.1.5

- `ctrl+e` opens the selected task in the editor, so the whole list is reachable without the mouse.

Everything from 0.1.4 is included: the custom `/todo` dialog with state and priority tabs, tags, sorting, search, paging, per-cell clicks, the two-row editor with priority and due chips, `PgUp`/`PgDn`/`Home`/`End`, the `▸` cursor with the current row in bold and the compact sidebar strip.

![The sidebar strip](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeonVeganMan/opencode-todo-md/master/screen/sidebar.png)

## Tools

`todo_write` and `todo_read` keep the file in sync with the agent: full-list writes, or patches by stable id (`{ "id": 3, "status": "completed" }`). Priorities, due dates, creation and completion dates live in an invisible HTML comment, so the markdown stays clean and hand edits keep working.

## Notes

Installing registers the tools; nothing forces the model to use them. One line in `AGENTS.md` makes the file the source of truth:

```markdown
If the project has a TODO.md at the root, keep it updated with todo_write (run todo_read first, then send the whole list).
```

49 unit tests. MIT.
